notes:
### New
- **Theme: Match OS theme.** Light or dark as your computer is set, and it
  changes along with it. It is also a step in the first-start setup.
- **Deck EQ knobs run low to high:** LOW is now on the left and HI on the right (they were the other way round). What each knob does is unchanged.
- **More preferences, like Engine DJ's:** Settings → **Analysis** has a BPM
  range, key notation (Sharps, Flats, Open Key or Camelot) and **Find missing
  keys**. Settings → **Audio → Sound format** sets sample rate, buffer size
  and output channel pair. Settings → **Player & mixer → Playback** sets where
  a loaded track starts, the sync mode (Bar / Beat / Tempo) and sync button,
  quantize for new cues and loops, static or dynamic time, and the waveform
  zoom. Settings → **Library** chooses whether to show and sync hot cues,
  memory cues or both.
- **Comment column:** the track list can show each song's comment (right-click
  the column headers → Comment), and you can edit it in place like title or
  artist.
- **Your own tags:** right-click songs → **Tags ▸** to tick tags (or make a
  new one). A tag belongs to the song, so it shows in Rekordbox, Engine DJ and
  OpenCrate's own library alike. Type `#tagname` in the search box to find
  songs with a tag. Rename or delete tags in Settings → Tags. The Tags column
  in the track list is hidden at first (right-click the headers). Tags live in
  OpenCrate only for now: they aren't written into Rekordbox, Engine DJ or
  your files. When OpenCrate converts or relinks a song, its tags follow the
  new file, and the **Edit info…** dialog has a Tags row.
- **Smart playlists:** right-click a library → **New smart playlist…** and
  set rules (tag, BPM, key, rating, genre, year, date added, comment, in a
  playlist, …) matching all or any. The playlist fills itself, always up to
  date, with a live "N songs match" while you edit, suggestions for genre,
  artist, album and label values, and the song count in the sidebar.
- **Tidy → Files → Duplicates** finds audio files that are exact copies of each
  other (like `Song.aiff` and `Song-1.aiff`) across Rekordbox, Engine DJ and
  OpenCrate, shows which copy stays, and removes the extras from OpenCrate's
  library and, following the "Changes go to" switches, Engine DJ's and
  Rekordbox's: their playlist places, rating (and for OpenCrate and Engine DJ
  cues and tags) move to the copy that stays, and files no library lists any
  more go to the Trash. In Rekordbox the extra tracks themselves stay in the
  collection for now. **Undo last removal** restores the libraries.
- **Fake lossless check** (part of Tidy → Files → Health): finds
  FLAC, WAV and AIFF files whose sound stops at a sharp cutoff, the sign of an
  MP3 saved as lossless, and says what it looks like ("about 128 kbps MP3").
  It only reads files.
- **Tidy asks less when your libraries are kept in step:** with *Keep
  everything in step* on (and Rekordbox and Engine DJ both switched on for
  Tidy's changes), there is no library to choose and no tick boxes: Tidy works
  on everything and one line says so.
- **First-start setup:** on a new install, a short pop-up walks through six
  choices (one library or separate ones, file backups, automatic analysis and
  key notation, default conversion format, theme, track list size with a
  preview), each with a
  recommended pick already selected. Skip it any time; Settings → General →
  *Run setup again* shows it again. Existing installs don't get it by themselves.
- **Tidy is easier to find your way around:** instead of ten tabs, its tools
  are listed on the left in three groups, each with a line saying what it
  does: Tags (Smart fixes, Genres & artists, Find tags online), Files (Health,
  Duplicates, Moved files, Artwork) and USB stick. Drag the list's edge to
  change its width.

### Fixed
- **Dropdowns open in one place:** every dropdown menu now opens directly below its
  control, as wide as it, with the current choice ticked (the system's own popup
  jumped around depending on the choice).
- **Missing covers and Tag lookup lists:** a song that OpenCrate's library lists
  more than once no longer breaks the list (it stayed empty and the other parts
  of the screen stopped responding). Each file is listed once.
